evidence_status: Local reproducible evidence for pre-existing state-lock symlinks and cross-rename inode migration; not a publisher signature, zero-knowledge proof, hostile-OS defense or distributed-lock proof.

criteria.evidence: New final and dangling lock-symlink processes exit 2 with an explicit symbolic-link diagnostic. They do not poll to completion, create a report, consume a directive, replace state or create a dangling target.

In the old two-process symlink case the first process remains alive after state replacement while the second exits 0 and changes pending/consumed from 6/0 to 5/1; the lock symlink resolves to the replacement state inode. Both new processes exit 2 and the initial state bytes and inode remain unchanged.

Regular and hard-link sidecar cases retain exclusion across save_atomic on both binaries: the first process remains alive, the second exits 2 with state-is-already-locked, and pending/consumed stay 6/0. The regular sidecar remains a separate stable inode; the hard-link sidecar remains on the initial state inode rather than migrating to the replacement.

The independent source check confirms the portable symlink_metadata rejection and that Unix OpenOptions custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) is applied before options.open; acquisition then uses try_lock_exclusive and propagates other errors.

verify-lock-symlink-python.py independently reconstructs file types, link targets, target and link identities, SHA-256 values, v4 transitions, process liveness and FIFO report bytes. Five filesystem known answers and six synthetic fake-report rejections run before the real five-case report is accepted.

The normal old/new control produces byte-identical state and report files. The complete gate passes 109 Rust tests and nine independent Python oracle entries; wave, execution, replay, output-path, atomic-write, cognitive and smoke anchors do not drift.

The implementation commit was archived into a directory without .git and built with an initially absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR. build-all exited 0; the resulting clean binary generated the final differential, whose new-binary hash equals the clean binary hash.

development_corrections.record: The first exploratory fixture read a nonexistent pending field instead of v4 directives and stopped before attack execution. The second printed the exploit but incorrectly expected six directives after consuming one; it was corrected to five and rerun from scratch before CONFIRMED was recorded.

The first differential setup incorrectly demanded byte equality with qfos-exec-pre-state despite using a different Registry policy identity. It stopped after fixture setup, before the attack process. The replacement checks the preregistered v4 6/0 shape, while the independent oracle requires one common initial hash across every old/new case.

The independent oracle initially conflated unchanged state bytes with an unchanged inode for regular and hard-link rename cases, then incorrectly compared a hard-link sidecar with its pre-arm lock. These oracle errors rejected the real report; the predicates were split and anchored to the armed sidecar, followed by full self-test and real-report reruns.
One outer /bin/sh invocation rejected set -o pipefail before the gate started. It was rerun explicitly under bash; only the latter complete log is counted as a gate result.

not_proven: The repair rejects symbolic-link sidecars but does not prevent replacement of a regular lock pathname after acquisition, constrain non-cooperating writers or provide a distributed/cross-host lock.
The portable precheck alone is not claimed to close non-Unix check/open races; Unix uses O_NOFOLLOW for the actual open. No non-Unix runtime differential was executed.
No CAS, WAL, fsync, crash-power-loss durability, hostile-OS confinement or post-create ledger-temporary race defense is added.

This local PASS does not establish publisher authentication, external delivery or ACK, federation activation, external QF-OS/QIOS compatibility, formal execution proof, zero-knowledge proof, a new push or external CI.
